the intensity of grief reported by gay men who had experienced three or more losses was not related to the number of losses experienced.

there is no relationship between the number and intensity of losses experienced by a group of gay men who had lost at last three friends or relatives to AIDS and the intensity of their bereavement response.

there was no significant relationship found between the number of losses and the intensity of the grief experienced, but there were relationships among social and demographics variables and intensity of grief.

the relationship between the numbers of losses experienced by gay men from AIDS and the intensity of their grief response.
the impact of AIDS on the gay male community.
the impact of multiple loss on the bereavement process of gay men.

the intensity of grief among this sample of gay men was not associated with the number of losses experienced.
the number of individual AIDS losses is not related to the intensity of grief, but that the number of losses may influence the intensity of grief in some way.
multiple loss and cumulative loss do occur among gay men, and that they are associated with the intensity of grief and other situational factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of losses is not the most significant factor in the intensity of grief.
gay men in this study were experiencing multiple losses from the AIDS epidemic and that the intensity of their grief was not related to the number of losses.
multiple loss is not necessarily associated with more intense grief among gay men who have lost friends, lovers, and relatives to AIDS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be aware of and sensitive to the multiple losses that gay men experience from the HIV/AIDS epidemic and the cumulative effect of those losses on the intensity of their grief.
we need to be aware of the potential for multiple losses and cumulative grief among gay men and other men who have sex with men (MSM).
